argument_summary: The certification defense should be narrowed. The admissible record supports that the current release passed aggregate readiness by 2.4 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, but it also shows a current health-plan benefits support slice regression below the warning threshold and shows that prior approval and the informal monitoring comment do not satisfy the current-release policy burden. The supportable position is therefore not unqualified compliance; it is a narrow, caveated certification basis that relies on current-release disclosure of the regression as a material limitation and on post-launch monitoring as a risk-management follow-through rather than as a substitute for required disclosure or approved mitigation.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is clear that current release documentation must reflect current evaluation results and that material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation. The same admissible evidence also permits a narrower reading favorable to certification: aggregate pass and no severity-one incidents remain relevant launch-readiness evidence, while the subgroup regression must be treated as a disclosed limitation rather than ignored or backfilled by stale approval. Prior approval from nine weeks earlier and the release-thread monitoring note can be used as context only, not as policy substitutes.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim about business cost is needed to resolve the audit issue. The narrower certification framing reduces unnecessary escalation by aligning the packet to the policy standard instead of overstating what stale approval or informal monitoring can cover.
concessions: The current record does not support an unqualified claim that the release already satisfies the documentation requirement.
The health-plan benefits support slice regression is current adverse evidence for a named use case and cannot be minimized away.
The informal monitoring comment is not an approved mitigation or risk acceptance.
The prior approved release predates the current corpus refresh and eval batch, so it cannot provide current-release coverage.
